question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
option_1: Alka bought new pair of shoes for the party.
option_2: He was an honest engineer by profession.
option_3: Suhas has a younger brother and an elder sister.
option_4: It was a huge zoo with an elephant enclosure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Alka bought new pair of shoes for the party.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence in Option 1 is incorrect because the singular countable noun phrase "pair of shoes" needs the indefinite article 'a' before it. It should be "Alka bought a new pair of shoes for the party."

◦ Correct: Alka bought a new pair of shoes for the party.

• "Pair" is a singular countable noun, so it must be preceded by an article or a determiner (a pair, this pair, one pair).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is correct — "an honest engineer" rightly uses "an" because "honest" begins with a vowel sound (the 'h' is silent).

• Option 3 is correct — "a younger brother and an elder sister" uses the articles properly ("elder" begins with a vowel sound).

• Option 4 is correct — "a huge zoo" and "an elephant enclosure" both use the articles correctly.

NOTE

• Article rule: use "a/an" before a singular countable noun mentioned for the first time. The choice between "a" and "an" depends on the sound, not the spelling — a university, an hour, an honest man, a European.

question:
Select the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

His remarks made the matter worse.
option_4: Killed two birds with one stone
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Added fuel to the fire.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to add fuel to the fire" means to make a bad situation even worse; to worsen a matter/conflict. (आग में घी डालना)

◦ Correct: His remarks added fuel to the fire.

• Since the underlined segment is "made the matter worse", this idiom is the perfect substitute.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Spilled the beans" means to reveal a secret. (भेद खोल देना)

• Option 3 "Made a splash" means to attract a lot of attention suddenly.

• Option 4 "Killed two birds with one stone" means to achieve two aims with a single action. (एक तीर से दो निशाने)

NOTE

• Similar idioms of worsening a situation: "fan the flames", "rub salt into the wound", "pour oil on the fire".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The athletes / trained tirelessness / to prepare for / the upcoming competition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. trained tirelessness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "trained" must be modified by an adverb, not a noun. "Tirelessness" is a noun; the correct word is the adverb "tirelessly" (without getting tired).

◦ Correct: The athletes trained tirelessly to prepare for the upcoming competition.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "The athletes" (subject), "to prepare for" (infinitive of purpose) and "the upcoming competition" (object) are all grammatically correct.

• Word family: tireless (adjective — अथक), tirelessly (adverb), tirelessness (noun).

NOTE

• Rule: an adverb (usually formed by adding "-ly" to the adjective) modifies a verb — worked hard, ran quickly, trained tirelessly. A noun cannot modify a verb in this way.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the INCORRECT spelling in the given sentence.

Pleasee allow me to start.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Please.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Pleasee" in the sentence is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Please" — used to make a polite request. (कृपया)

◦ Correct: Please allow me to start.

• Spelling key: P + LEASE — only one final "e".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "Pleeasse", 2 "Pleesse" and 4 "Pleasse" are all incorrect spellings with wrongly doubled letters.

NOTE

• Related words: please (verb/interjection), pleasant (adjective), pleasure (noun), pleasing (adjective). Watch the single "s" in "please" and "pleasure".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The storm caused extensive damage to homes, ___________ many families homeless.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. leaving.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When a clause expresses the result/consequence of the action in the main clause, the present participle (V-ing) is used. The storm caused damage, with the result that many families became homeless — "leaving many families homeless".

◦ Correct: The storm caused extensive damage to homes, leaving many families homeless.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "to leave" (infinitive of purpose) wrongly suggests the storm intended to make families homeless.

• Option 2 "leave" (base form) cannot follow a comma without a subject and auxiliary.

• Option 3 "is left" (passive) does not fit the structure at all.

NOTE

• The participle of result is common in SSC: "It rained heavily, flooding the streets"; "The company shut down, rendering hundreds jobless".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He is / an expert / in / an English literature.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. an English literature.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Literature" is an uncountable (abstract) noun, so it does NOT take the indefinite article "an". The segment should simply be "English literature".

◦ Correct: He is an expert in English literature.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "He is" (subject + verb), "an expert" (correct use of "an" before a vowel sound) and "in" (correct preposition after "expert") are all correct.

• We say "expert in/at a subject or field" — an expert in physics, an expert at chess.

NOTE

• Uncountable nouns that never take "a/an": information, advice, furniture, luggage, news, knowledge, literature, poetry, scenery, work.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Grease someone's palm
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To bribe someone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to grease someone's palm" means to give someone money dishonestly to get something done; to bribe someone. (रिश्वत देना / मुट्ठी गरम करना)

◦ Example: He greased the clerk's palm to get his file cleared quickly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To flatter someone" is expressed by idioms like "butter someone up".

• Option 2 "To beat someone" and Option 3 "To abuse someone" have no connection with this idiom.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "oil someone's palm" (same meaning), "under the table" (secret/illegal payment), "kickback" (illegal commission). Frequently asked in SSC CGL/CHSL/MTS idiom questions.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The elusive moon peeked from behind the clouds, illuminating the earth with its gentle glow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. lighting up the earth with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Illuminating" means providing light; making bright. Its closest substitute is "lighting up" — the moon was lighting up the earth with its gentle glow. (प्रकाशित करना / रोशन करना)

◦ Correct: The elusive moon peeked from behind the clouds, lighting up the earth with its gentle glow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "glowing up the earth for" uses the wrong verb pattern and wrong preposition ("for" instead of "with").

• Option 2 "empowering" (giving power/authority) and Option 4 "encouraging" (giving hope/confidence) change the meaning completely.

NOTE

• Synonyms of illuminate: light up, brighten, irradiate, illumine. "Elusive" means difficult to find or catch (मायावी); "peeked" means looked quickly/appeared briefly.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Admited.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Admited" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Admitted" — with a double 't'. (स्वीकार किया / प्रवेश दिया)

• Rule: when a verb ends in a single vowel + single consonant and the last syllable is stressed, the final consonant is doubled before "-ed/-ing": admit → admitted, occur → occurred, permit → permitted.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Admittance" (permission to enter), "Admissible" (acceptable, allowable — as of evidence) and "Admission" (entry; acknowledgement) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Compare: begin → beginning, prefer → preferred, refer → referred; but open → opened, visit → visited (stress on the first syllable, so no doubling).

question:
Select the correct spelling of the incorrectly spelt word in the given sentence.

He was suspended from the party due to his suspiscious activities.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Suspicious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "suspiscious" in the sentence is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Suspicious", meaning causing a feeling that something is wrong or dishonest; doubtful. (संदेहजनक / संदिग्ध)

◦ Correct: He was suspended from the party due to his suspicious activities.

• Spelling key: SUS + PI + CIOUS (no extra "s" before "cious").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "Suspicius", 2 "Suspitious" and 3 "Suspeceous" are all incorrect spellings.

• Word family: suspect (verb/noun), suspicion (noun), suspicious (adjective), suspiciously (adverb).

NOTE

• Common "-cious" words asked in SSC: delicious, gracious, spacious, precious, ferocious, tenacious, suspicious. Compare "-tious" words: ambitious, cautious, nutritious.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Ambrosial
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Malodorous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ambrosial" means extremely pleasing to the taste or smell; delicious, fragrant (like ambrosia, the food of the gods). (सुगंधित / अति स्वादिष्ट)

• Its antonym is "Malodorous", meaning having a very unpleasant smell; foul-smelling. (दुर्गंधयुक्त)

◦ Example: The ambrosial aroma of the kitchen contrasted with the malodorous drain outside.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Faithful" (loyal) and Option 3 "Vengeful" (seeking revenge) are unrelated.

• Option 2 "Pleasing" is a synonym of ambrosial, not an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of ambrosial: fragrant, aromatic, delicious, heavenly, delectable. Antonyms: malodorous, foul, fetid, rancid, stinking. Prefix "mal-" = bad (malfunction, malnutrition, malpractice).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Frugal
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Profligate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Frugal" means careful in spending money; economical; sparing. (मितव्ययी)

• Its antonym is "Profligate", meaning recklessly extravagant or wasteful in spending. (फ़िज़ूलख़र्च / अपव्ययी)

◦ Example: His frugal habits saved him, while his profligate brother wasted the family fortune.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Thrifty" is a synonym of frugal.

• Option 1 "Cheap" (inexpensive / miserly) and Option 4 "Happy" do not express the opposite of frugal.

NOTE

• Synonyms of frugal: thrifty, economical, sparing, parsimonious. Antonyms: profligate, extravagant, wasteful, spendthrift, prodigal.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase.

Those who have died cannot be brought back to life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Resurrect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Resurrect" means to bring back to life; to restore (a dead person) to life or to revive something forgotten/disused. (पुनर्जीवित करना)

◦ The phrase "brought back to life" exactly matches the meaning of "resurrect".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Retract" means to withdraw a statement or promise. (वापस लेना)

• Option 3 "Abstract" means to take away/summarise; as an adjective, existing in thought only.

• Option 4 "Extract" means to remove or take out something. (निकालना)

NOTE

• Related words: resurrection (noun — coming back to life), revive (bring back to consciousness/use), resuscitate (revive from unconsciousness). Prefix "re-" = again/back.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Hermetic
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Esoteric.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hermetic" means (1) airtight/sealed completely, and (2) obscure, mysterious, understood only by a select few. In the second sense, its closest synonym is "Esoteric" — intended for or understood by only a small group with special knowledge. (गूढ़ / रहस्यमय)

◦ Example: The philosopher's hermetic/esoteric writings baffled ordinary readers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Intelligible" (able to be understood) and Option 3 "Lucid" (clear, easy to understand) are antonyms of hermetic.

• Option 2 "Obnoxious" (extremely unpleasant) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of esoteric/hermetic: abstruse, arcane, cryptic, recondite, occult. Antonyms: simple, clear, lucid, intelligible, exoteric.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

she had garnered the information from various books.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Dispersed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Garnered" means gathered or collected (information, support, etc.). (एकत्र किया / बटोरा)

• Its antonym is "Dispersed", meaning scattered in different directions; distributed widely. (बिखेरा / तितर-बितर किया)

◦ Example: She garnered facts from many books, but the notes got dispersed later.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Criticised" (found fault with), Option 2 "Implemented" (put into effect) and Option 4 "Liberated" (set free) do not convey the opposite of "collected".

NOTE

• Synonyms of garner: gather, collect, accumulate, amass, acquire. Antonyms: disperse, scatter, dissipate, distribute, squander.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical/spelling error.

He was lying at / his bed when he / saw the snake entering / through the window.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. He way lying at.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the first segment "He was lying at". The correct preposition with "bed" (as a surface) is "on" — "lying on his bed", not "lying at his bed".

◦ Correct: He was lying on his bed when he saw the snake entering through the window.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "his bed when he", "saw the snake entering" and "through the window" are all grammatically correct.

• "Lie – lay – lain – lying" (to rest/recline) vs "lay – laid – laid – laying" (to place something). Here "was lying" (past continuous of "lie") is correctly formed; only the preposition is wrong.

NOTE

• Prepositions of place: "on the bed / on the table" (surface), "in bed" (idiomatic — sleeping/resting), "at the door / at the station" (point). "He was lying on his bed" or "He was in bed" are both correct.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She is learning / to play the guitar / to pursue her passion / for the music.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. for the music.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Music" used in a general sense is an uncountable/abstract noun and does NOT take the definite article "the". The segment should be "for music", not "for the music".

◦ Correct: She is learning to play the guitar to pursue her passion for music.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "She is learning" (present continuous), "to play the guitar" (the article "the" IS correctly used before names of musical instruments — play the guitar/the piano/the violin) and "to pursue her passion" are all correct.

• "Passion for something" is the correct preposition pattern.

NOTE

• Rule: use "the" with musical instruments (play the flute) but NOT with abstract nouns used generally (love music, passion for music, fond of art).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

A raven, which you know is black as coal, was envious of the swan, because her feathers are as white as the purest snow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. feathers were as white as.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main clause is in the past tense ("was envious"), so the reason clause must also be in the past tense — "because her feathers were as white as the purest snow" (tense consistency).

• "Feathers" is plural, so it takes the plural verb "were", and the comparison structure "as white as" must be kept intact.

◦ Correct: ... was envious of the swan, because her feathers were as white as the purest snow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 and 3 use "is" — a singular, present-tense verb — which fails both in number and in tense.

• Option 4 "was a white as" uses a singular verb with a plural subject and breaks the "as ... as" structure.

NOTE

• The comparison of equality is "as + adjective + as": as white as snow, as black as coal, as busy as a bee. In narration, keep all clauses in the same time frame (sequence of tenses).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Vivid
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Bright.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Vivid" means very bright, intense or strong (of colours/light); producing clear and powerful images in the mind (of memories/descriptions). Its closest synonym is "bright". (चमकीला / सजीव)

◦ Example: The painting was full of vivid/bright colours.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "Dull" (not bright) is the antonym of vivid.

• Option 1 "Varied" (diverse) and Option 2 "Soothing" (calming) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of vivid: bright, brilliant, intense, graphic, lifelike, striking. Antonyms: dull, faint, dim, colourless, vague.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Do you know the purpose of a fire extinguisher? It helps to put up with an engulfing fire, in case of an emergency.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. put out.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "put out" means to extinguish (a fire, light, cigarette). A fire extinguisher helps to put out a fire. (बुझाना)

◦ Correct: It helps to put out an engulfing fire, in case of an emergency.

• "Put up with" means "to tolerate", which makes no sense with a fire extinguisher.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "run away with" (to steal / to win easily), Option 2 "turn over" (to flip; to hand over) and Option 3 "stand out" (to be noticeable) do not fit.

NOTE

• Important "put" phrasal verbs for SSC: put out (extinguish), put off (postpone), put up with (tolerate), put on (wear), put down (suppress/write down), put forward (propose).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Khashaba Jadhav was the independent India's first individual olympic medallist. There (1) _________ some firsts that stay in history forever. The one held by Khashaba Jadhav is one such first. He might have been referred to as the Pocket Dynamo, but his deeds dwarfed those of far (2) _________ athletes in his sport. Just a couple of years after India had become a Republic, Jadhav took part in the 1952 Olympics at Helsinki, Finland. As funding sportspersons weren't really a (3) _________ for a country just finding its feet, Jadhav's trip to Helsinki was actually funded by the public. Jadhav however, (4) _________ his way to fame, becoming independent India's first individual Olympic medal winner. He (5) _________ bronze in the bantamweight category.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. are.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject after "There" is "some firsts" — a plural noun. The relative clause "that stay in history forever" is in the present tense, so the sentence states a general truth. Hence the plural, present-tense verb "are" is required.

◦ Correct: There are some firsts that stay in history forever.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "is" is singular; Option 2 "was" is singular and past; Option 3 "were" is past tense — all clash with the plural subject and the present-tense general statement.

• In "There + be" constructions, the verb agrees with the noun that follows: There is a book / There are some books.

NOTE

• Universal truths and general statements take the simple present tense: "There are moments that define history." Khashaba Jadhav won independent India's first individual Olympic medal (bronze in wrestling, Helsinki 1952).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Khashaba Jadhav was the independent India's first individual olympic medallist. There (1) _________ some firsts that stay in history forever. The one held by Khashaba Jadhav is one such first. He might have been referred to as the Pocket Dynamo, but his deeds dwarfed those of far (2) _________ athletes in his sport. Just a couple of years after India had become a Republic, Jadhav took part in the 1952 Olympics at Helsinki, Finland. As funding sportspersons weren't really a (3) _________ for a country just finding its feet, Jadhav's trip to Helsinki was actually funded by the public. Jadhav however, (4) _________ his way to fame, becoming independent India's first individual Olympic medal winner. He (5) _________ bronze in the bantamweight category.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. bigger.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The intensifier "far" before the blank signals a comparative degree — "far bigger athletes". The contrast is that though Jadhav was small (the "Pocket Dynamo"), his deeds dwarfed those of much bigger athletes.

◦ Correct: ... his deeds dwarfed those of far bigger athletes in his sport.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "big" and 3 "small" are positive degree forms and cannot follow "far" in a comparison.

• Option 1 "smaller" is comparative but reverses the intended contrast — he was the small one whose deeds outshone the big ones.

• "Dwarfed" means made to seem small by comparison.

NOTE

• "Far/much/even/still + comparative" is a standard intensifying pattern: far bigger, much better, even stronger. "Pocket Dynamo" was Khashaba Jadhav's nickname because of his small build and explosive energy.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Khashaba Jadhav was the independent India's first individual olympic medallist. There (1) _________ some firsts that stay in history forever. The one held by Khashaba Jadhav is one such first. He might have been referred to as the Pocket Dynamo, but his deeds dwarfed those of far (2) _________ athletes in his sport. Just a couple of years after India had become a Republic, Jadhav took part in the 1952 Olympics at Helsinki, Finland. As funding sportspersons weren't really a (3) _________ for a country just finding its feet, Jadhav's trip to Helsinki was actually funded by the public. Jadhav however, (4) _________ his way to fame, becoming independent India's first individual Olympic medal winner. He (5) _________ bronze in the bantamweight category.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 3.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. priority.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Priority" means something regarded as more important than other things. For a newly independent country "just finding its feet", funding sportspersons was not a priority. (प्राथमिकता)

◦ Correct: As funding sportspersons weren't really a priority for a country just finding its feet ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "posteriority" (the state of coming after) and Option 4 "subsequence" (the state of following) are the opposites of priority and make no sense here.

• Option 3 "supremacy" (the state of being supreme/dominant) does not fit the context of government spending choices.

NOTE

• "Finding its feet" is an idiom meaning becoming established/confident in a new situation. Because the government could not fund him, Jadhav's Helsinki trip was financed by public contributions.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Khashaba Jadhav was the independent India's first individual olympic medallist. There (1) _________ some firsts that stay in history forever. The one held by Khashaba Jadhav is one such first. He might have been referred to as the Pocket Dynamo, but his deeds dwarfed those of far (2) _________ athletes in his sport. Just a couple of years after India had become a Republic, Jadhav took part in the 1952 Olympics at Helsinki, Finland. As funding sportspersons weren't really a (3) _________ for a country just finding its feet, Jadhav's trip to Helsinki was actually funded by the public. Jadhav however, (4) _________ his way to fame, becoming independent India's first individual Olympic medal winner. He (5) _________ bronze in the bantamweight category.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 4.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. wrestled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Khashaba Jadhav was a wrestler, so he "wrestled his way to fame" — i.e., achieved fame through wrestling. The verb also fits the idiomatic pattern "verb + one's way to" (fought his way to, worked his way up). (कुश्ती लड़कर प्रसिद्धि पाई)

◦ Correct: Jadhav however, wrestled his way to fame, becoming independent India's first individual Olympic medal winner.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "buckled-under" (gave way under pressure), Option 3 "Lazed" (relaxed idly) and Option 4 "Surrendered" (gave up) all contradict the idea of triumph.

NOTE

• Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav won the bronze medal in freestyle wrestling (bantamweight) at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics — independent India's first individual Olympic medal. He was posthumously awarded the Arjuna Award in 2000.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Khashaba Jadhav was the independent India's first individual olympic medallist. There (1) _________ some firsts that stay in history forever. The one held by Khashaba Jadhav is one such first. He might have been referred to as the Pocket Dynamo, but his deeds dwarfed those of far (2) _________ athletes in his sport. Just a couple of years after India had become a Republic, Jadhav took part in the 1952 Olympics at Helsinki, Finland. As funding sportspersons weren't really a (3) _________ for a country just finding its feet, Jadhav's trip to Helsinki was actually funded by the public. Jadhav however, (4) _________ his way to fame, becoming independent India's first individual Olympic medal winner. He (5) _________ bronze in the bantamweight category.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. claimed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Claimed" here means won/secured (a medal, title or prize). "He claimed bronze in the bantamweight category" is the natural sports collocation. (जीता / हासिल किया)

◦ Correct: He claimed bronze in the bantamweight category.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "lulled" (soothed to sleep), Option 2 "constructed" (built) and Option 4 "forgave" (pardoned) are meaningless with "bronze".

• Common sports collocations: claim/clinch/bag/win a medal, claim a title, claim victory.

NOTE

• Bantamweight is a lower weight category in wrestling/boxing. Jadhav's bronze at Helsinki 1952 came in the freestyle wrestling bantamweight (57 kg) class; India's next individual Olympic medal came only in 1996 (Leander Paes, tennis).

question: The official journey of 'Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav' commenced on:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 12th March 2021.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The official journey of "Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav" commenced on 12 March 2021, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off a symbolic 'Dandi March' from Sabarmati Ashram, Ahmedabad. (आज़ादी का अमृत महोत्सव — 12 मार्च 2021)

• The date marked the start of a 75-week countdown to the 75th anniversary of Independence (15 August 2022).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav was an initiative of the Government of India to celebrate 75 years of independence and the glorious history of India's people, culture and achievements.

• 12 March was chosen because Mahatma Gandhi began the historic Dandi (Salt) March on 12 March 1930.

NOTE

• The celebrations formally continued up to 15 August 2023, and were followed by the "Meri Maati Mera Desh" campaign as the finale.

question:
Rank the following states in ascending order, based on their population density, as per Census 2011.

Tripura, Meghalaya, Manipur, Nagaland
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland-Manipur-Meghalaya-Tripura.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, the population densities (persons per sq km) of these north-eastern states are approximately:

◦ Nagaland — 119

◦ Manipur — 128

◦ Meghalaya — 132

◦ Tripura — 350

• Hence, in ascending order: Nagaland < Manipur < Meghalaya < Tripura.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Population density = total population ÷ total area (persons per sq km). India's average density as per Census 2011 was 382 persons per sq km.

• Bihar (1,106) had the highest density among states, and Arunachal Pradesh (17) the lowest; among UTs, Delhi (11,320) was the highest.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was India's 15th Census (7th after independence); the Census is conducted every 10 years by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

question: In which of the following states can the 'Loo' phenomenon be observed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Loo" is a strong, hot and dry local wind that blows over the plains of north and north-west India — especially Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh — during the summer months of May and June. (लू — गर्म व शुष्क स्थानीय पवन)

• Direct exposure to the Loo can cause heat stroke (sunstroke), which may even be fatal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Goa, Tamil Nadu and Manipur do not experience the Loo — their climates are moderated by the sea or by hilly terrain.

• Other local winds of India: "Kalbaisakhi" (violent pre-monsoon thunderstorms of West Bengal/Assam), "Mango showers" (pre-monsoon showers of Kerala–Karnataka coast), "Blossom showers" (help coffee blossom in Karnataka).

NOTE

• World local winds asked in SSC: Chinook (warm wind, Rockies), Foehn (warm wind, Alps), Mistral (cold wind, France), Sirocco (hot wind from Sahara).

question: Who is literate according to the Census of India?
option_1: A person above 14 years of age, who can read and write with understanding in any language.
option_2: A person above 5 years of age, who can read and write with understanding in any language.
option_3: A person above 7 years of age, who can read and write with understanding in any language.
option_4: A person above 18 years of age, who can read and write with understanding in any language.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A person above 7 years of age, who can read and write with understanding in any language.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India, a person aged 7 years and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language is treated as literate. (साक्षर — 7 वर्ष या अधिक आयु, किसी भी भाषा में समझ के साथ पढ़ना-लिखना)

• A person who can only read but cannot write is not counted as literate.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• As per Census 2011, India's literacy rate was 74.04% (males 82.14%, females 65.46%).

• Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate (94%) and Bihar the lowest (61.8%) among states.

NOTE

• The 7-years-and-above criterion has been used since the 1991 Census; earlier Censuses counted persons aged 5 and above. Formal education is NOT necessary — only the ability to read and write with understanding.

question: Which of the following awards and recognitions was NOT received by Vempati Chinna Satyam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Shri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vempati Chinna Satyam (1929–2012) was a legendary Kuchipudi dance guru from Andhra Pradesh. He received the Padma Bhushan (1998) — NOT the Padma Shri. (वेम्पति चिन्ना सत्यम — कुचिपुड़ी गुरु)

• He was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1981), the Kalidas Samman (Madhya Pradesh government) and honorary doctorates from universities.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• He founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy at Chennai (1963) and systematised and popularised Kuchipudi worldwide, training thousands of dancers including several film actresses.

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, named after the village Kuchipudi in the Krishna district; it traces its tradition to Siddhendra Yogi.

NOTE

• The eight recognised classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: The East India Company lost all its administrative powers with the enforcement of ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Government of India Act, 1858.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the Revolt of 1857, the British Parliament passed the Government of India Act, 1858, by which the East India Company lost all its administrative powers and the governance of India was transferred directly to the British Crown. (भारत शासन अधिनियम, 1858)

• The office of the Secretary of State for India (assisted by a 15-member Council of India) was created, and the Governor-General of India was given the additional title of Viceroy — Lord Canning became the first Viceroy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Regulating Act, 1773 — first parliamentary regulation of the Company; made Warren Hastings Governor-General of Bengal and set up the Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774).

• The Charter Act of 1853 — introduced open competition for the civil services and separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's Council.

• The Indian Councils Act, 1892 — enlarged legislative councils and introduced an element of indirect election.

NOTE

• The 1858 Act is also called the "Act for the Good Government of India". Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1 November 1858) announced the new policy; she later took the title "Empress of India" in 1876.

question: A three-time Olympian, PT Usha broke the Asian Games record in four events (200 m, 400 m, 400 m hurdles and 4 × 400 m relay) in ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seoul, 1986.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the 1986 Asian Games in Seoul (South Korea), P. T. Usha won four gold medals and one silver, breaking the Asian Games records in the 200 m, 400 m, 400 m hurdles and 4 × 400 m relay. (पी. टी. उषा — सियोल एशियाई खेल 1986)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• P. T. Usha, known as the "Payyoli Express" and the "Queen of Indian track and field", hails from Kerala. At the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics she missed the bronze in the 400 m hurdles by just 1/100th of a second.

• She received the Arjuna Award and Padma Shri (1985), and in 2022 she became the President of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) — the first woman to hold the post; she was also nominated to the Rajya Sabha.

NOTE

• The Asian Games are held every four years under the Olympic Council of Asia; the first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in 1951.

question: In which state of India is the Telaiya dam located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Tilaiya (Telaiya) dam is located on the Barakar River in the Koderma district of Jharkhand. (तिलैया बांध — बराकर नदी, झारखंड)

• It was the first dam and hydroelectric station built by the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC), commissioned in 1953.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The DVC was established on 7 July 1948 as independent India's first multipurpose river valley project, modelled on the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) of the USA.

• Other DVC dams: Konar (Konar river), Maithon and Panchet (Barakar/Damodar rivers).

• The Barakar is the main tributary of the Damodar River, which is known as the "Sorrow of Bengal" for its past floods.

NOTE

• Important dams for SSC: Bhakra Nangal (Sutlej, HP/Punjab), Hirakud (Mahanadi, Odisha — longest dam), Tehri (Bhagirathi, Uttarakhand — highest dam), Sardar Sarovar (Narmada, Gujarat).

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the contingency fund of India?
option_2: It is issued on behalf of the President of India.
option_4: Allowances and emoluments of the President are charged under it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Allowances and emoluments of the President are charged under it.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The emoluments and allowances of the President are NOT charged on the Contingency Fund — they are "charged expenditure" on the Consolidated Fund of India (Article 112(3)). Hence Option 4 is NOT a feature of the Contingency Fund. (राष्ट्रपति के वेतन-भत्ते — भारत की संचित निधि पर भारित)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Contingency Fund of India is established under Article 267 of the Constitution (by the Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950).

• It is placed at the disposal of the President, who can make advances out of it to meet unforeseen/emergency expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament.

• It is operated by the Finance Secretary on behalf of the President; the amounts drawn are later recouped from the Consolidated Fund after Parliament's approval.

NOTE

• Three funds of the Government of India: Consolidated Fund (Article 266(1)) — all revenues and loans; Public Account (Article 266(2)) — money held in trust; Contingency Fund (Article 267) — emergencies. The corpus of the Contingency Fund was raised from Rs 500 crore to Rs 30,000 crore in 2021-22.

question: The autobiography of which of the following famous Indian musicians is titled 'My Life, My Music'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ravi Shankar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "My Music, My Life" is the autobiography of the legendary sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar (first published in 1968). (पंडित रविशंकर — सितार वादक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Pandit Ravi Shankar (1920–2012) popularised Indian classical music in the West, collaborating with violinist Yehudi Menuhin and The Beatles' George Harrison. He also wrote "Raga Mala" (a later autobiography).

• He was honoured with the Bharat Ratna (1999), three Padma awards and multiple Grammy Awards; he was also a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha.

• Shivkumar Sharma — santoor maestro; Zakir Hussain — tabla maestro; Bismillah Khan — shehnai maestro (Bharat Ratna 2001).

NOTE

• Musician–instrument pairs for SSC: Ravi Shankar (sitar), Bismillah Khan (shehnai), Shivkumar Sharma (santoor), Hariprasad Chaurasia (flute), Zakir Hussain & Alla Rakha (tabla), Amjad Ali Khan (sarod).

question: As of February 2023, who is the Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitin Gadkari.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of February 2023, Nitin Gadkari was the Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways. He has held this portfolio since 2014 and represents the Nagpur (Maharashtra) Lok Sabha constituency. (नितिन गडकरी — सड़क परिवहन और राजमार्ग मंत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• At that time: Dharmendra Pradhan — Minister of Education and Skill Development; Mansukh Mandaviya — Minister of Health and Family Welfare; Ashwini Vaishnaw — Minister of Railways, Communications, and Electronics & IT.

• The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways implements flagship programmes such as Bharatmala Pariyojana and oversees the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

NOTE

• Nitin Gadkari is associated with major expressway projects (e.g., the Delhi–Mumbai Expressway) and initiatives for ethanol/flex-fuel vehicles and green mobility.

question: Who does NOT fall under the executive of the Indian Union?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chief Justice of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Chief Justice of India (CJI) heads the judiciary, not the executive. Hence the CJI does NOT fall under the Union executive. (भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश — न्यायपालिका)

• The Union Executive (Part V, Articles 52–78 of the Constitution) consists of the President, the Vice-President, the Prime Minister, the Council of Ministers and the Attorney-General of India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The President is the nominal/constitutional head (Article 52); the real executive power is exercised by the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister (Article 74).

• The CJI and the Supreme Court derive their authority from Articles 124–147; the judiciary is kept independent of the executive and the legislature (separation of powers).

NOTE

• Article 50 (Directive Principle) directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State.

question: Which of the following dances is performed in Goa during the festival Ganesh Chaturthi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fugdi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fugdi" is a popular folk dance of Goa (and the Konkan region) performed by women, especially during Ganesh Chaturthi and other religious/festive occasions. The dancers form circles or rows and whirl at a fast tempo while singing. (फुगड़ी — गोवा का लोकनृत्य, गणेश चतुर्थी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Tarangmel — a colourful, energetic group dance of Goan youth performed with flags and streamers during Dussehra and Holi.

• Dhalo — a Goan folk dance performed by women at night in the month of Paush.

• Dhangar — a devotional dance of the Dhangar (shepherd) community of Goa, performed during Navratri.

NOTE

• Other famous Goan folk forms: Dekhni, Lamp dance (Divli), Ghode Modni, Corridinho (Portuguese-influenced). Ganesh Chaturthi (Chovoth) is one of the biggest festivals of Goa and Maharashtra.

question: Moseley observed that the plot of √v against atomic number (Z) gave a straigth line. What does v indicate here?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Frequency of X-rays emitted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1913, Henry Moseley studied the characteristic X-ray spectra of elements. He found that the plot of the square root of the frequency (√ν) of the characteristic X-rays emitted against the atomic number (Z) of the element is a straight line. (मोज़ले का नियम — अभिलाक्षणिक X-किरणों की आवृत्ति)

• Moseley's law: √ν = a(Z − b), where a and b are constants for a given spectral series.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Moseley's work showed that the atomic number (Z), not the atomic mass, is the fundamental property of an element — this corrected anomalies in Mendeleev's periodic table (e.g., Ar–K, Co–Ni) and gave the Modern Periodic Law: properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.

• α-rays are helium nuclei, β-rays are fast electrons and γ-rays are high-energy electromagnetic radiation — none of these is what Moseley plotted.

NOTE

• X-rays were discovered by W. C. Roentgen (1895), who received the first Nobel Prize in Physics (1901). Moseley died young in World War I (1915) and never received a Nobel Prize.

question: At which Olympic games did India receive its first Olympic medal in a shooting event?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Athens 2004.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India won its first Olympic medal in shooting at the Athens Olympics 2004, when Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore won the silver medal in the men's double trap event. (एथेंस 2004 — राज्यवर्धन सिंह राठौड़, रजत पदक)

• It was also independent India's first individual silver medal at the Olympics.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• At Beijing 2008, Abhinav Bindra won gold in the 10 m air rifle — India's first individual Olympic gold medal.

• At London 2012, shooters Vijay Kumar (silver, 25 m rapid fire pistol) and Gagan Narang (bronze, 10 m air rifle) won medals.

• Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore later became the Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports.

NOTE

• At Paris 2024, Manu Bhaker became the first Indian woman to win an Olympic shooting medal (bronze, 10 m air pistol) and won two medals in a single Games. Shooting at the Olympics is governed by the ISSF rules.

question: When a river reaches a low lying plain, it continues erosion of soil as well as deposition and as a result of both these factors another river channel develops and later it is detached from the main river forming a U-shaped lake; this is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is an oxbow lake.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In its lower/middle course over a flat plain, a river flows in loops called meanders. Continuous erosion on the outer bank and deposition on the inner bank make the meander loop increasingly curved; eventually the river cuts across the narrow neck and the loop is detached from the main channel, forming a U-shaped (horseshoe-shaped) lake called an oxbow lake. (गोखुर/छाड़न झील)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Canal" is a man-made waterway; "estuary" is the tidal mouth of a river where it meets the sea; "gulf" is a large sea inlet — none of these is formed by meander cut-off.

• Oxbow lakes are common in the Ganga plains (e.g., in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh).

NOTE

• Depositional features of a river: flood plains, levees, meanders, oxbow lakes, deltas. Erosional features: V-shaped valleys, gorges, canyons, waterfalls, potholes.

question: Fa-Hsien, a Chinese Buddhist Pilgrim, began his journey back home (China) from ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fa-Hsien (Faxian), the Chinese Buddhist pilgrim who visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) of the Gupta dynasty (c. 399–414 CE), began his return journey to China by sea from the port of Tamralipti in Bengal. (फाह्यान — ताम्रलिप्ति, बंगाल से वापसी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Fa-Hsien came to India overland through Central Asia to collect Buddhist texts; he spent years at Pataliputra copying scriptures and described Gupta-era society in his account "Fo-Kwo-Ki (A Record of Buddhist Kingdoms)".

• From Tamralipti he sailed to Sri Lanka (Ceylon) and then via Java back to China.

• Tamralipti (modern Tamluk, West Bengal) was a famous ancient port on the Bay of Bengal.

NOTE

• Chinese pilgrims to India: Fa-Hsien (Gupta period, Chandragupta II), Hiuen Tsang/Xuanzang ("Prince of Pilgrims", during Harshavardhana, 7th century) and I-tsing/Yijing (studied at Nalanda, late 7th century).

question: When was the first-round table Conference started by the British Government in London?
solution_text:
The correct answer is November 1930.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The First Round Table Conference was inaugurated in London on 12 November 1930 by King George V and chaired by British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald. It was convened to discuss the recommendations of the Simon Commission and constitutional reforms for India. (प्रथम गोलमेज़ सम्मेलन — नवंबर 1930)

• The Indian National Congress boycotted it because of the ongoing Civil Disobedience Movement; its leaders were in jail.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Second Round Table Conference (September–December 1931) — the Congress participated, with Mahatma Gandhi as its sole representative, following the Gandhi–Irwin Pact (5 March 1931); it failed over the issue of communal representation.

• Third Round Table Conference (November–December 1932) — again not attended by the Congress; its discussions contributed to the Government of India Act, 1935.

• Participants of the first conference included the Muslim League, the princely states, and Dr B. R. Ambedkar (representing the depressed classes).

NOTE

• Sequence for SSC: Simon Commission (1928) → Nehru Report (1928) → Lahore Session/Purna Swaraj (1929) → Dandi March & Civil Disobedience (1930) → three Round Table Conferences (1930, 1931, 1932) → Communal Award (1932) → Poona Pact (1932) → Government of India Act (1935).

question: Which of the following is the role of fibre in the diet?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Promoting digestion and bowel regularity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dietary fibre (roughage) adds bulk to food, helps the smooth movement of food through the digestive tract, promotes digestion, prevents constipation and ensures bowel regularity. (आहार रेशा — पाचन एवं मल त्याग में सहायता)

• Fibre is the indigestible part of plant foods — mainly cellulose — as humans lack the enzyme to digest it.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sources of fibre: whole grains, fruits, green leafy vegetables, salads, pulses and nuts.

• Fibre also helps control blood sugar and cholesterol and gives a feeling of fullness, aiding weight management.

• Body temperature is regulated by the skin and hypothalamus (helped by water), and quick energy is provided by carbohydrates (glucose) — not by fibre.

NOTE

• Components of a balanced diet: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water and roughage (fibre). Though fibre provides no nutrients, it is essential for healthy digestion.

question: Lalita J Rao is associated with which of the following gharanas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agra gharana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lalita J. Rao (Lalith J. Rao) is a renowned Hindustani classical vocalist of the "Agra gharana". She trained under masters of the gharana such as Pt. Ramarao Naik and Pt. Dinkar Kaikini. (ललिता जे. राव — आगरा घराना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Agra gharana is one of the oldest gharanas of Hindustani (khayal) vocal music; its most celebrated exponent was Ustad Faiyaz Khan, honoured with the title "Aftab-e-Mausiqi" (Sun of Music).

• Other gharanas and exponents: Kirana — Abdul Karim Khan, Bhimsen Joshi, Gangubai Hangal; Jaipur-Atrauli — Alladiya Khan, Kesarbai Kerkar, Kishori Amonkar; Benaras — Girija Devi (thumri); Gwalior — the oldest khayal gharana.

NOTE

• A "gharana" is a lineage/school of Hindustani music with a distinctive style of singing or playing, usually named after the place of its origin.

question: Which of the following is a unitary feature of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is single citizenship.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Single citizenship" is a unitary feature of the Indian Constitution — every Indian is a citizen of India only, with no separate state citizenship (unlike the USA, which has dual citizenship of the nation and the state). (एकल नागरिकता — एकात्मक लक्षण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Federal features of the Indian Constitution: division of powers between Centre and states (Seventh Schedule), a written and rigid Constitution, supremacy of the Constitution, bicameralism (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) and an independent judiciary.

• Other unitary features: a strong Centre, single Constitution, single integrated judiciary, All-India Services, appointment of Governors by the Centre, Emergency provisions, and Parliament's power to alter state boundaries (Article 3).

• That is why India is described as "federal in form but unitary in spirit" or a "quasi-federal" state (K. C. Wheare); Article 1 calls India a "Union of States".

NOTE

• Citizenship is dealt with in Part II (Articles 5–11) of the Constitution and the Citizenship Act, 1955 (acquisition by birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory).

question: 'Rajatarangini', a vivid account of the kings of Kashmir, was composed by Kalhana in the ______ language.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanskrit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rajatarangini" ("The River of Kings") was composed by Kalhana in the Sanskrit language in the 12th century CE (c. 1148–1150). It is a long verse chronicle of the kings of Kashmir. (राजतरंगिणी — कल्हण, संस्कृत)

• It is regarded as the first proper historical work of ancient India, showing a critical, near-modern sense of history.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kalhana wrote it during the reign of King Jayasimha of the Lohara dynasty of Kashmir; the work contains eight tarangas (books/waves).

• It was later continued by Jonaraja and Srivara, and translated into Persian under Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir; Aurel Stein translated it into English.

NOTE

• Famous Sanskrit works for SSC: Arthashastra (Kautilya), Ashtadhyayi (Panini), Mudrarakshasa (Vishakhadatta), Harshacharita (Banabhatta), Kumarasambhava & Abhijnanashakuntalam (Kalidasa), Rajatarangini (Kalhana).

question:
Which of the following options correctly matches column-A with column-B?

Column-A (Common name): i. Cuttle Fish, ii. Silver fish, iii. Devil fish, iv. Cat fish

Column-B (Scientific name): a. Siluriformes, b. Mobula, c. Sepia, d. Lepisma
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-c, ii-d, iii-b, iv-a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct matching of common names with scientific names is:

◦ Cuttle fish — Sepia (a marine mollusc of class Cephalopoda; not a true fish)

◦ Silver fish — Lepisma (a wingless household insect of class Insecta; not a true fish)

◦ Devil fish — Mobula (the devil ray, a cartilaginous fish related to the manta ray)

◦ Cat fish — Siluriformes (the order of true bony fishes with whisker-like barbels)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Cuttle fish", "silver fish", "jelly fish" and "star fish" are misnomers — despite the word "fish" in their names, they are not true fishes.

• Sepia produces the dark ink used for defence; Lepisma saccharina feeds on starch in books and clothes; Mobula rays are called devil fish because of their horn-like cephalic fins.

NOTE

• Classification tip for SSC: true fishes belong to classes Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous — sharks, rays) and Osteichthyes (bony — catfish, rohu); jellyfish (Coelenterata), starfish (Echinodermata), cuttlefish (Mollusca) and silverfish (Arthropoda/Insecta) are NOT fishes.

question: Sultan Ghari tomb is situated to west of the Qutub in Delhi is like a fortress within a walled enclosure with bastions on the comers, with its ____________ grave chamber underground.
solution_text:
The correct answer is octagonal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sultan Ghari tomb, situated to the west of the Qutub complex in Delhi, looks like a fortress within a walled enclosure with bastions at the corners, and has its octagonal grave chamber underground (in a crypt — "ghari" means cave). (सुल्तान ग़ारी का मक़बरा — अष्टकोणीय भूमिगत कब्र कक्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sultan Ghari was built in 1231 CE by Sultan Iltutmish for his eldest son and heir-apparent, Prince Nasiruddin Mahmud.

• It is regarded as the first Islamic mausoleum (tomb) built in India.

• Iltutmish (r. 1211–1236) of the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty also completed the Qutub Minar, introduced the silver tanka and copper jital, and organised the Turkan-i-Chahalgani (corps of forty nobles).

NOTE

• The octagonal tomb design later became a regular feature of the tombs of the Sayyid and Lodi periods in Delhi.

question: 'The Climate Smart Cities Assessment Framework 2.0' is to evaluate how many cities across India?
solution_text:

IMPORTANT POINTS

Additional Information

• The CSCAF assesses cities across five thematic areas: (i) Energy and Green Buildings, (ii) Urban Planning, Green Cover and Biodiversity, (iii) Mobility and Air Quality, (iv) Water Management, and (v) Waste Management — with 28 indicators.

• It works under the Smart Cities Mission, which was launched on 25 June 2015 to develop 100 citizen-friendly and sustainable smart cities.

• The framework aims to provide cities a roadmap for combating climate change while planning their investments.
